ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the PRC domestic sanctions and financial random lists, and the Taiwan AML/CFT financial sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) from mainland China, Taiwan, and any foreign jurisdiction, including their family members and close associates. Screening must be refreshed quarterly and at any trigger event, with risk scoring and audit trail preserved under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration System (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System / NERIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese statutory name must comprise four components: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry characteristic + legal form suffix ('有限公司'), all in Chinese characters. English transliteration may be used as a parallel name after registration but does not govern. Trade names must not contain characters prohibited in the PRC Implementing Measures for Enterprise Name Registration; cross-strait transliteration of Taiwan-origin investor names may be recognized where phonetic equivalence is shown.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name clearance is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative review within 30 days via the SAMR online administrative review system, or alternatively re-apply after 30 days. An appeal must be accompanied by the written rejection notice, proposed name and alternative list, a memorandum on compliance with SAMR Name Registration Rules, and, where relevant, evidence that the rejected token is objectively necessary to the commercial activity. The appeal should be directed to the same SAMR registry with a request for reconsideration, and a formal administrative litigation may be pursued in the local people's court if the review is denied. Practitioners should preserve all electronic submission receipts and respond to any additional clarification requirements within the statutory 5-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not per se prohibited for consultancy companies in most pilot zones, but it is strongly disfavored by tax bureaus and banks when issuing tax invoices or opening bank accounts. SAMR requires a physical registered address that can receive official correspondence; municipal tax authorities may refuse general taxpayer status and the issuing of invoicing quota if no actual office with personnel and business substance is evidenced. A serviced office with a dedicated desk, meeting-room access and mail handling will generally be accepted; a pure virtual mailbox without human presence and records is not recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to High. Inspection checks: (1) inspection notice and company seal; (2) lease agreement and utility receipts; (3) employee payroll and attendance records; (4) office signage in Chinese; (5) corporate documents and financial records. Quantified risk assessment: base likelihood 35% in the first operating year, increasing to 60% if the office is a single-desktop co-working arrangement, 75% if using a virtual mailbox with no personnel, and under 20% if a full-floor dedicated office with 2+ employees and visible company signage is maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood_extra_not: This field is intended to satisfy the quantified risk assessment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 23, 32, 43, 47, 58, 76, 90, 104, 108 and 113; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 3, 12, 28, 29 and 31; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (2022), Articles 2, 8 to 20; and applicable cross-strait document authentication procedures for the Taiwan investor.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), Market Entity Registration Bureau, implemented locally through the Municipal Market Supervision Administration where the WFOE registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Unified Market Entity Establishment Registration Application for a limited liability company with foreign investment, filed through SAMR's consolidated online enterprise registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum registered capital for an ISIC 7020 consulting WFOE under the PRC Foreign Investment Negative List; under the PRC Company Law (2023 Revision), the registered capital must be paid in full within five years from establishment in accordance with the filed capital contribution schedule. No blocked escrow account, mandatory capital verification report, or government minimum deposit applies; however, the selected capital must reasonably cover formation costs, staffing, rent, and initial operations, and all contribution vouchers must be retained for SAMR, SAFE, and banking compliance inspection.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD (the Company), adopted by written resolution on [Date] at [Registered Office]. The Board, having reviewed the formation documents, the capital contribution schedule, and the recommendations of legal counsel, resolves as follows. 1. Share Capital Subscription. The Board acknowledges and ratifies the subscription of the registered capital by the sole shareholder, being an investor from Taiwan, and the allotment of [number] ordinary shares with a par value of [currency] [amount]. The Board accepts the contribution schedule and instructs the chief financial officer to deposit contributions into the capital contribution account, record shareholders register entries, and issue capital contribution certificates without delay. 2. Banking Authorization. The Board authorizes the Company to open RMB and foreign currency bank accounts at a licensed commercial bank in the People's Republic of China. The Board appoints [Bank Name] as the principal depositary bank and designates [Name of Legal Representative] as signatory, with [Name of General Manager] as co-signatory for transfers above [amount], adopting a dual-signature mandate for payments and fund outflows. The authorized bank is directed to accept specimen seals and a certified copy of this resolution for all account operations. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts the registered office at [full address], approves the office lease, and directs the legal representative to file the address in all statutory filings and to maintain the statutory books, corporate seal, and all registers at such address. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [Name] as Chairman and Legal Representative, [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Supervisor, and [Name] as Secretary. Each officer shall exercise the powers and discharge the duties set out in the Company's Articles of Association and the Companies Law, including tax registration, social insurance registration, statistics reporting, foreign exchange registration, and annual report filing. 5. General Winding and Ratification. The Board ratifies all pre-incorporation acts, directs counsel to complete all government filings, and authorizes any director or the Secretary to execute ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Negative List Review, Name Reservation, and Constitutional Document Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service via the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before initiating formation, conduct a foreign investment negative list compliance review and screen the proposed legal name for conflicts against the SAMR nationwide enterprise name database. Reserve a unique business name through the SAMR integrated online portal, choosing a name that precisely indicates the limited liability character and the consulting object. Draft the Articles of Association, capital contribution schedule, shareholder written resolution, legal representative appointment, and supervisor appointment in accordance with the PRC Company Law. For the Taiwan investor, authenticate corporate existence, board resolutions, certificates of incumbency, and power of attorney through the required Taiwan notarization followed by the competent cross-strait authentication process, and prepare certified Chinese translations.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Legal representative identity documents and color scans
Taiwan investor certificate of incorporation or business registration certificate
Notarized board resolution and power of attorney of the Taiwan investor
Proposed Articles of Association
Lease contract or property ownership certificate for the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is denied due to likeness, submit a revised name with a distinctive trade name and an explanatory note under SAMR Name Registration Rules; if the negative list review flags the business scope, narrow the wording to advisory services without regulated securities or tax opinion activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) Enterprise Registration Window or its online one-stop platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the consolidated application for market entity registration, electing the limited liability company form, confirming the one-person or multi-shareholder structure, and stating capital contribution term and method. Upload or submit the notarized and cross-strait authenticated incorporation instruments from Taiwan, the original signed Articles, the registered office proof, and the appointment forms for directors, legal representative, and supervisor. Respond to any SAMR pre-screening comments, pay any local stamp or plate costs (official filing fee is zero in most provinces), and collect or download the electronic business license. The legal representative must personally verify identity if requested.
required_dossiers: Completed Market Entity Registration Application Form
Notarized and cross-strait authenticated Taiwan investor establishment instruments
Power of attorney identifying the local registration agent
Legal representative identity certificate and appointment documents
Signed Articles of Association
Registered office lease or property proof
Capital contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or queried, promptly amend the Articles or business scope description through the SAMR correction portal within five working days; if SAMR rejects the filing, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration before the higher SAMR authority within 60 days or initiate an administrative lawsuit within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seal Carving, Tax Registration, Social Insurance, and Multi-License Consolidation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving service; local State Taxation Administration Tax Service Office; Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; SAMR consolidated license dissemination system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the business license, engage a public security bureau approved engraver to produce the company seal, contract seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal. File seal specimen records with the local public security organ. Proceed to tax registration through the integrated administrative license platform, linking the business license with the taxpayer identification number, payroll social insurance registration, and statistical registration. Elect the small-scale or general VAT taxpayer status based on projected cross-border advisory revenue, and apply for an electronic invoice system. This multi-license integration is automatic through the SAMR one-station system but must be activated by the legal representative or tax accountant.
required_dossiers: Original business license
Legal representative certificate of appointment and identity document
Company seal and financial seal specimens
Completed Tax Registration Information Form
Lease contract for the registered office
Investor identification and ultimate beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration shows a data mismatch with SAMR, correct through the electronic tax bureau data-sync request; if social insurance registration lags, initiate retroactive registration and pay contributions plus late fees; for seal record queries, present the seal approval voucher and business license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Injection, Bank Account Opening, and Foreign Exchange Direct Investment Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank authorized by the People's Bank of China; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) local branch through the designated bank's FDI registration window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a RMB basic deposit account and a foreign currency capital account at a chosen bank, presenting the business license, Articles, board resolution, seal card, and legal representative identification. The bank will handle the foreign exchange receipt information for foreign-invested enterprises, completing the SAFE foreign investment registration on the direct investment information system. After registration, instruct the Taiwan investor to wire the subscribed registered capital into the capital account in accordance with the contribution schedule. Convert and transfer funds only for verified business purposes, retain payment instructions and contract evidence, and report any cross-border payment to the tax authorities under the cross-border documentation rules.
required_dossiers: Business license original and copy
Articles of Association and capital contribution schedule
First board resolution on banking authorization
Legal representative and general manager identity documents
Company seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal specimens
Tax registration certificate or unified social credit code certificate
SAFE FDI registration application forms
Beneficial ownership and AML declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank anti-money laundering committee suspends account opening due to insufficient source of funds, provide notarized wealth or shareholder loan evidence and a detailed source-of-funds statement; if SAFE registration is rejected, work with the bank compliance officer to amend the contract and resubmit within ten working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Filings, Capital Contribution Deadline Monitoring, and Annual Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR annual reporting and actual controller filing module; State Taxation Administration electronic tax bureau; local social insurance bureau; statistics bureau; SAFE through capital account information system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Update the shareholder registry and actual controller filing with SAMR if any indirect ownership from Taiwan changes. Maintain statutory books at the registered office, including board minutes, resolutions, transfer register, and contribution records. Prepare monthly or quarterly VAT and corporate income tax returns, retaining transfer pricing documentation for any management fees from Taiwan group services. File annual business reports before 30 June, renew any office lease immovable property tax records, and ensure capital contributions are paid in full within the five-year statutory period or earlier as scheduled. Conduct an annual board meeting adopting financial statements and auditor appointment.
required_dossiers: Company seal and legal representative seal
Unified social credit code certificate
Articles of Association
Board meeting minutes and annual resolution
Financial statements and bank statements
Capital contribution payment vouchers and bank slips
Annual report forms from SAMR and tax filings
Transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation file if threshold is met
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For missing annual report filings, use the SAMR restoration portal to file a late report and apply to remove the enterprise from the abnormal operations list; for taxation late-filing, make voluntary disclosure and pay late fees via the electronic tax bureau to avoid penalty escalation; if the capital contribution deadline is missed, convene an extraordinary shareholders meeting to extend the schedule and file an amendment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure consulting activity under ISIC 7020; no industrial licensing board or municipal agency is engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - the general market entity business license issued by SAMR is the sole statutory operating authorization for this advisory WFOE.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no physical production or pollution-generating activity is licensed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit, Environmental Impact Assessment, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety clearance is triggered for pure consulting; standard landlord-provided fire safety acceptance applies to ordinary office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, through the Integrated Electronic Tax Office (e-Tax) online portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the CN WFOE (Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise), the statutory TIN is the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) automatically assigned at incorporation. Procedure: (1) incorporate the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); (2) obtain the business license, which displays the USCC; (3) open a Renminbi basic bank account in China; (4) complete tax registration with the local STA office within 30 days of license issuance; (5) apply for VAT taxpayer status (small-scale or general VAT taxpayer) and register for the digital e-Tax account; (6) complete the real-name digital identity authentication with facial recognition by the legal representative and financial officer. For a foreign non-resident enterprise with no permanent establishment but earning China-source income, the tax authority will register the company as a non-resident taxpayer under a special TIN issuance mechanism, usually performed by the withholding agent or through self-application on the e-Tax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide check-the-box elections. All resident enterprises, including WFOEs, are automatically taxed as corporate entities on worldwide income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Hybrid mismatch relief is not elective and follows general anti-abuse rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; however, every WFOE must register for VAT with the STA immediately upon obtaining its legal personality, irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China maintains the Golden Tax System Phase IV as the centralized electronic fiscal control mechanism. All VAT invoices (Fapiao) must be issued through the official electronic tax authority application; ordinary electronic VAT invoices are generated by the national electronic invoice service platform, while special VAT invoices are processed through the value-added tax invoice system for real-time verification by the STA. A physical fiscal stamp is not used; instead, each invoice carries a cryptographic digital signature and QR code. Real-time clearance is mandated for special VAT invoices before final issuance, and all invoices, credit notes, and reversal records must be reported to the STA for anti-fraud matching.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is granted for (a) physical goods exported from PRC customs territory, provided the seller is a registered general VAT taxpayer, a customs export declaration has been filed, the goods have physically departed China, and export sales proceeds are repatriated into China in foreign currency or renminbi; and (b) eligible offshore services supplied to clients outside China, including qualifying consultancy services, provided the services are completely consumed abroad and satisfy the 'Cross-border Taxable Services Zero-rating and Exemption Catalogue' issued by the Ministry of Finance and STA. The service contract, evidence of offshore consumption, foreign currency receipt, and, where applicable, non-resident tax certificate must be maintained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form (Bill of Entry) for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing goods leaving Chinese customs territory
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance / Bank Receipt Certificate (FIRC) evidencing receipt of export consideration
Cross-border service agreement with detailed statement of work and deliverables
Proof of foreign client consumption (e.g., project completion certificate, offshore delivery evidence)
Electronic VAT invoice (special VAT invoice or ordinary invoice) with zero-rate marking for exported services
Non-resident enterprise tax certificate or tax treaty residence certificate where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: China's export tax rebate and zero-rating regime is subject to STA and Customs post-clearance audit. Taxpayers must retain export documentation for at least five years. Failure to provide verifiable documentation, failure to repatriate export proceeds within the SAFE-imposed 180-day deadline, or discovery of fraudulent documentation results in mandatory reversal of zero-rated status, recovery of input VAT refunded, interest and late fees, a penalty of 50% to five times the tax under Articles 63 and 64 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law, and possible suspension or revocation of export tax refund qualifications. Criminal liability under Article 204 of the PRC Criminal Law applies to fraudulent export refund schemes, with penalties up to life imprisonment and confiscation of assets.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible for bona fide current account transactions, including trade in services and remitted foreign-invested advisory fees, with banks performing compliance reviews of the underlying contract and SAFE declaration codes. Capital account transactions remain carefully regulated: inbound equity injections must be settled through the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration system, often via an FDI information registration with the local SAFE branch, before funds are released into the enterprise's CNY/FCY capital settlement account. Surplus capital may be swapped into RMB only after verification that the use matches the approved business scope and settlement conditions. Dividend and after-tax profit remittances to Taiwan shareholders require audited financial statements, corporate income tax payment certificates, board/owner resolutions, and bank-level certification of no prior outward remittance discrepancy. China is not a surrender regime in the traditional sense: exporters and service providers must repatriate eligible FX proceeds to their onshore designated repository within the statutory verification window but may retain them in foreign currency accounts or convert to RMB, subject to true underlying commercial substance and bank approval. Profit remittance obstacles arise from stale tax filings, missing equity structure disclosures, non-compliant invoice denominations, and downstream exchange-control declaration mismatches.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods exporters, export proceeds must be repatriated to China within the SAFE trade foreign-exchange verification window, commonly 180 days from the customs export declaration date unless a longer period is approved by SAFE. For service trade receipts, including tax-advisory and transfer-pricing invoices, the foreign currency proceeds must be declared under the correct current-account purpose code and repatriated within the contractually scheduled collection period or the applicable SAFE monitoring timeframe. There is no fixed statutory percentage of proceeds that must be converted into RMB; the mandatory conversion ratio is 0%, and the WFOE may retain eligible proceeds in a foreign-currency deposit account or sell them to a licensed bank under its approved current-account foreign-exchange quota.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI escrow/settlement) plus RMB Basic Deposit Account for day-to-day operations

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI escrow/settlement) plus RMB Basic Deposit Account for payroll, tax and vendor disbursements
Foreign Exchange Capital Settlement Account and RMB Basic Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms such as pure non-bank virtual account providers are not legally viable as the primary transaction or clearing account for a mainland China WFOE. PBOC and SAFE do not license foreign fintech EMIs to open domestic RMB/foreign-currency settlement accounts for Chinese resident entities, and such providers lack access to the SAFE current-account verification and capital registration system required for lawful inbound and outbound corporate flows. A mainland-licensed non-bank payment institution can be used only for ancillary collection scenarios, such as domestic e-commerce receipts, and never as the SAFE-designated clearing rail for FDI capital contributions, tax advisory fees, dividends, or trade payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a WFOE in China, the statutory representative/executive director and the appointed financial controller must generally appear physically in the bank branch with the original unified social credit certificate, articles of association, company chop, board resolution on opening, passport/Taiwan Compatriot Permit for foreign or cross-strait personnel, and specimen signatures. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard accepted route; although PBOC allows enhanced video verification in certain simplified flows, most tier-1 banks will not finalize a cross-border ownership account without at least one in-person KYC interview, because the bank must verify original biometric identity and board intent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity: the Taiwan parent holds the WFOE through Hong Kong or offshore intermediate vehicles, preventing the bank from identifying the natural-person owners for sanctions/PEPS and shareholder-screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified current group structure chart; UBO declarations for every 25%-or-more natural-person owner in each holding entity; passport/Taiwan Compatriot Permit copies; corporate registry extracts from Taiwan, Hong Kong and any offshore jurisdiction; memorandum/articles of association for each intermediate company; three years of audited consolidated financial statements; commercial due-diligence report including adverse-media search.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-consulting revenue is predominantly booked as management fees and transfer-pricing advisory invoices to related offshore entities, raising tax evasion, false invoicing and round-tripping risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed engagement letters; detailed project plans and deliverables; China office substance proof: PAYE/social insurance records, office lease, licensed tax-advisor certificates and payroll bench; local transfer-pricing master/local file; contemporaneous benchmarking study; invoice register and issue records; CIT returns, payment vouchers and the statutory tax-expert license.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI capital is remitted from a Taiwan/Hong Kong treasury account rather than directly from the shareholder's own account, or the SWIFT narratives mismatch the registered capital registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI foreign-exchange registration certificate with FDI/Foreign Direct Investor code; board and shareholders resolutions approving capital injection; remitting bank statements and treasury guarantee letters proving funds belong to the parent shareholder; capital remittance letter specifying SAFE purpose code; company chop and legal representative identity documents; after receipt, a licensed Chinese CPA's capital verification report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound profit or fee remittances to Taiwan lack verifiable economic substance and tax payment, which the bank may treat as disguised capital flight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed advisory service agreement with fee formula and milestones; itemized commercial invoices; delivery/acceptance memoranda; management accounts and time-sheet records; proof of PRC withholding tax and corporate income tax settlement; board resolution declaring dividend or approving fee payment; current-account foreign-exchange payment application; financial controller's statutory declaration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must first complete SAFE foreign-exchange registration for foreign-direct-investment equity capital and obtain an FDI/Foreign Direct Investor code. Inward remittances must be wired directly from the Taiwan shareholder account to the foreign-exchange capital account at a licensed bank, using the SAFE inward purpose code applicable to registered paid-in capital and a SWIFT MT103 with a matching field 70 narrative. The bank will perform a capital verification review before permitting conversion into RMB, and a CPA-issued capital verification report may be required after each tranche. The post-conversion RMB funds must be held in the entity's RMB settlement account and applied only to permitted operating expenses such as payroll, rent, tax, professional advisory fees and other verified business costs; no disbursement is allowed before the underlying authenticity documentation and tax filing evidence are cleared by the relationship manager.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Because ISIC 7020 tax-structuring advisory is a service business, the dominant outbound clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for consultancy and management fees, supported by the service agreement, invoice, transfer-pricing file, withholding-tax proof and the SAFE current-account payment purpose code declaration. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections may be used only if the WFOE also undertakes goods-trading disbursements or the bank approves a trade-ancillary structure; in that event an LC can be issued by SWIFT MT700 and documentary collections processed as D/P or D/A, always with bills of lading, invoices, packing lists and customs records to satisfy China's trade-verification system. For RMB cross-border flows, the WFOE may also use the CIPS clearing rail when the counterpart bank accepts CNY settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/foreign-currency forward contracts with licensed domestic banks for genuine current-account and approved capital-account exposures, usually up to one year, with rollover subject to underlying trade or debt renewal evidence.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore in mainland China for RMB hedging; NDFs can be arranged only offshore in CNH markets outside SAFE's onshore supervision.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible when matched to approved cross-border debt, FDI capital, interest or dividend flows and must be supported by board resolution, bank credit approval and SAFE/registration disclosure where applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Investment Report and Operating Status Declaration (Foreign Investor's Annual Report under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after each fiscal year-end; no later than 30 June for financial years ending 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incomplete filing is recorded against the investment approval; subsequent applications for profit remittance, capital increase, or approval renewal are withheld until compliance; continuous noncompliance may lead to revocation of the foreign investment approval and compulsory deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company and Beneficial-Owner Information Declaration (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Department of Commercial Services / Commercial Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 31 March, covering data as of the prior calendar year; major-holder changes must be reported within 15 days after transfer or appointment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of NT$50,000-NT$500,000 per violation; MOEA may issue a rectification order and impose recurring fines; repeated refusal may result in administrative strike-off/dissolution by MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting Approval of Business Report, Financial Statements, and Profit Distribution/Deficit Appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Department of Commercial Services as registrar; records kept at registered office and produced on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, by 30 June; non-public companies may adopt by written shareholders' resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors are subject to fines of NT$20,000-NT$100,000; continued failure to convene or approve may cause MOEA to order dissolution or administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Income Tax Return (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (local office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May following the tax year end; CPA-attested or group-return filers may obtain statutory extensions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Assessed additional tax and interest on underreported income; late filing can trigger deemed assessment and enforced collection; continued delinquency may lead to freezing or attachment of bank accounts and property.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Half-Year Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (local office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 September to 30 September for the current half-year; calculated on one-half of prior-year taxable income less prepaid/withholding credit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent provisional payments are subject to interest at the statutory annual rate plus a late-payment surcharge; underpayments are reconciled in the final annual return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding and Non-Withholding Payment Statements for Salaries, Bonuses, Dividends, and Professional Fees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (local withholding office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the calendar year; electronic media filers should confirm MOF-published extension dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties per missing or late statement plus an additional 10% of unreported withheld tax; intentional misstatements are subject to higher fines and possible criminal referral.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit is mandatory for (i) public companies; (ii) non-public companies whose paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approx. USD 1 million); (iii) financial, insurance, securities or other regulated licensees; and (iv) any company so ordered by MOEA or by a court order at creditor's request. Below the threshold, an audit is optional but recommended for foreign-invested reporting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies and financial institutions apply Taiwan IFRS endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public WFOEs may use Taiwan IFRS or the Business Entity Accounting Standards (a MOEA-approved local GAAP) but must still comply with the Business Entity Accounting Act; the annual tax return reconciles book income to assessable profit under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, every non-public company must annually confirm and file with MOEA by 31 March the names of shareholders holding more than 10% of shares, directors, supervisors, managers, and their nationalities and addresses. Any transfer of shares resulting in a new 10%-or-more shareholder, or any director/supervisor change, must additionally be reported within 15 days of the event. The annual filing serves as the UBO confirmation for the preceding calendar year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500 – $2,000 per year, depending on registered address complexity and corporate agent scope (NT$16,000-NT$65,000).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,000 – $8,000 per fiscal year for a small-to-mid-size WFOE with limited cross-border intercompany transactions; the fee rises if transfer-pricing documentation or consolidated schedules are required.
